messages: Tamhini’s Q2 review is ours this week. Varun has cleared the other lines; the nine I asked Mahesh about are yours. Variance sheet first, then I’ll put his reasons and papers beside each line.

tasks.title: Finish the variance sheet
tasks.prompt: Varun set up the variance sheet for the nine lines and left eight boxes for you. Enter each change as a percentage of the comparison, to one decimal: (Q2 − comparison) ÷ comparison × 100, with a minus for a fall. Your sheet goes to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your variance sheet to Aditi?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your figures but not change them.

hints: Divide by the comparison, not by Q2. Varun’s revenue against Q1: (3,094.61 − 2,778.68) ÷ 2,778.68 × 100 = 11.4%.

notes.l1.ply: Revenue: up a fifth on last year. Over the threshold on both comparisons, so it needs a reason with a paper.
notes.l2.pq1: Materials: 10.2% and ₹140.25 lakh. Just over the 10% line against Q1, so this one counts.
notes.l3.pq1: Wages: 11.4% and ₹12.05 lakh on Q1, so over the line. Something changed in July.
notes.l4.pq1: Power: 9.3% on Q1 is under 10%, though the rupees (₹11.66 lakh) are over. A line crosses only when the % and the rupees are both over.
notes.l5.ply: Job work: 37.5% on last year against 9.3% on Q1. Keep the two side by side; the gap between them is the question.
notes.l6.ply: Contract labour: 24.3% on last year, nothing on Q1. Whatever changed was in place by April.
notes.l7.ply: Our fees: minus 100%, but only ₹4.41 lakh, so under the line. A nil where last year had a provision still needs a look.
notes.l8.ply: Depreciation: 10.3%, but only ₹7.34 lakh, so under the line. A machine came in this quarter; check that its depreciation did too.

tasks.note: Change % = (Q2 − comparison) ÷ comparison × 100. Figures in ₹ lakh.

tasks.title: Explain or query each line
tasks.prompt: Aditi has put Mahesh’s reason and papers beside each line. Say which comparison, if either, crosses our threshold and make your call: no query, or a query to Mahesh. The results, minutes, plant MIS, fixed-asset schedule and our fee letter are under Other papers. Your calls go to Aditi when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your line calls to Aditi?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: A line crosses only when the change is more than 10% and more than ₹10 lakh on the same comparison: Q1 or Q2 last year. A reason holds only when a paper backs it and it fits both comparisons.
Before you pass depreciation and the fees, read the board minutes, the fixed-asset schedule and our engagement letter.

fields.label: Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: the paper you checked and what it showed

items.label: Line 1 · Revenue from operations
items.note: Line 1: over on both, and explained. Vayuvega brings ₹258.53 lakh against nothing last year. On Q1 every domestic customer rose 9.3%, as pieces machined did. Kilimani now takes a full container every second month: two in Q2, one in Q1. No query.

items.label: Line 2 · Cost of materials consumed
items.note: Line 2: over on both, and it moved with output: 59.2% of manufactured sales in Q2, 59.4% in Q1, 58.7% a year ago. The working adds up, and Q1’s closing stock is Q2’s opening. No query.

items.label: Line 3 · Wages – workers
items.note: Line 3: over on both. From July each workman costs 9% more: the average gross goes from ₹21,600 to ₹23,540. Workmen on the rolls went from 163 to 168 (156 a year ago, plant MIS). Heads × rate gives ₹1,17,46,460 to the rupee. No query.

items.label: Line 4 · Power and fuel
items.note: Line 4: 9.3% on Q1 is under 10%; on last year, 21.3% and ₹24.08 lakh are both over. Units rose with production; cost per unit is flat on Q1 and up 2.4% on last year, from the higher contract demand since April. No query.

items.label: Line 5 · Job work charges
items.note: Line 5: over on last year, up 37.5% and ₹24.44 lakh. Mahesh says Kudalwadi’s rates went up on 1 July, yet Q2 rose only 9.3% on Q1, exactly with production. The reason doesn’t fit, and no rate letter came. Query.

items.label: Line 6 · Contract labour charges
items.note: Line 6: over on last year. Jadhavwadi billed 110 workers every month this year against 92 last year, at about 4% more per worker: 110 ÷ 92 × 1.04 is the 24.3%. Flat on Q1, as it should be. No query.

items.label: Line 7 · Payment to auditors
items.note: Line 7: under the threshold only because ₹4.41 lakh is small. Last year every quarter carried a provision; this year Q1 and Q2 carry nothing, while note 2 says policies are unchanged. Our fees didn’t stop. Query.

items.label: Line 8 · Depreciation and amortisation
items.note: Line 8: 10.3% but only ₹7.34 lakh, so under the threshold. The minutes say TC-35 was accepted on 12 August; the schedule still holds it in work-in-progress. ₹59,342 for 50 days is missing. Query.

items.label: Line 9 · Finance costs
items.note: Line 9: under on both and down, as the loans say. Term loan I fell by another ₹75 lakh on 30 June; cash-credit interest fell on Q1; term loan II and its processing fee add ₹1.31 lakh. No query.

tasks.title: Draft the query mail to Mahesh
tasks.prompt: Aditi wants one mail to Mahesh with a query for each line that needs one: job work, our fees and depreciation. Pick the right paragraph for each. She will read it before it goes.

lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Aditi. You can read your mail but not change it.

hints: Each query says what doesn’t fit and asks for the one paper or entry that settles it.

options.text: Job work (₹89.61 lakh): up 37.5% on Q2 last year but only 9.3% on Q1, in step with production, so no 1 July rate rise shows. Please send Kudalwadi’s rate letter and the quantities sent for heat treatment each quarter.
options.why: The letter shows when and by how much the rates moved; the quantities show how much more went out. Together they explain the ₹24.44 lakh, or show it is something else.

options.text: Job work (₹89.61 lakh): up 37.5% on Q2 last year, which Kudalwadi’s 1 July rate revision explains. Please confirm the new rates to us by mail, so that we can note the reason in our file and close this line.
options.why: A mail repeating the reason adds nothing. Q2 rose with production over Q1, so the July revision is not in these figures. We need the letter and the quantities.

options.text: Job work (₹89.61 lakh): up 37.5% on Q2 last year against 9.3% on Q1. Please send the Kudalwadi and Sakhare bills for July to September with their delivery challans, so that we can vouch each bill before we close this line.
options.why: That is vouching, which a review ordinarily doesn’t do. We ask and compare: the rate letter and the quantities answer the question.

options.text: Payment to auditors (nil): this is our own fee and well under our threshold, so we have not looked at it further. Nothing is needed from you for Q2, and the bills can be booked when they arrive.
options.why: Last year every quarter carried a provision; this year none, though the reviews go on and our letter puts each at ₹1.75 lakh.

options.text: Payment to auditors (nil): last year every quarter carried a provision for our fees (₹4.41 lakh in Q2), but Q1 and Q2 this year carry none. Please provide for the fees in each quarter, as you did last year.
options.why: Costs are booked in the period they belong to, billed or not, and note 2 says the policies haven’t changed. The two reviews alone are ₹3.50 lakh.

options.text: Payment to auditors (nil): please keep booking our fees when the bills arrive, and add a sentence to note 2 of the results saying that review and audit fees are now booked when they are billed.
options.why: That writes the change into the results instead of correcting it. Last year’s quarters were on accrual, and Q2 has to be comparable with them.

options.text: Depreciation (₹78.32 lakh): CNC TC-35 starts its regular production for Ashvaratha on 1 October, so please capitalise it from that day and begin its depreciation in Q3, as your fixed-asset schedule already says.
options.why: Depreciation starts when a machine is ready for use, not when its regular orders begin. TC-35 was accepted after its trial run on 12 August.

options.text: Depreciation (₹78.32 lakh): CNC TC-35 was invoiced on 18 July, as your fixed-asset schedule shows, so please capitalise it from 18 July and book its depreciation from that date to 30 September.
options.why: The invoice date says nothing about readiness. TC-35 was installed in Bay 4 and accepted after its trial run on 12 August; that is the date.

options.text: Depreciation (₹78.32 lakh): CNC TC-35 was accepted after its trial run on 12 August, yet it sits in capital work-in-progress at 30 September. Please capitalise it from 12 August and book its depreciation from then.
options.why: A machine ready for use is depreciated from that day, idle or busy. From 12 August to 30 September that is ₹59,342.

freeText.label: Your own sentence for the mail

tasks.title: Before Sudha signs
tasks.prompt: Before Sudha signs the review report, Aditi wants three things settled: the checklist, Mahesh’s two uncorrected items and the sentence for the report.
hints: A review ordinarily means enquiry and analytical procedures. Confirming, counting and vouching belong to the audit.

questions.text: Aditi’s checklist has ten points, and four of them belong to an audit, not to this review. Tick the six that belong in this review.

options.text: Read the minutes of the board meetings held during and after the quarter
options.why: Minutes are where things the numbers don’t show turn up. The 14 August minutes are how we learnt TC-35 was accepted.

options.text: Send balance confirmation letters to Tamhini’s customers and banks
options.why: Confirmations test the records themselves, and they wait for the year-end audit.

options.text: Agree the results to the trial balance for the quarter
options.why: The results must agree with the books before anything else on the list means much.

options.text: Ask whether any accounting policy or method has changed
options.why: A standard question, and this quarter it has an answer: fees booked when billed, not provided each quarter.

options.text: Attend a stock count at the Chakan plant for 30 September
options.why: Observing a count is audit work. A review ordinarily relies on enquiry and analytical procedures.

options.text: Ask about related-party transactions and compliance with loan covenants
options.why: Both are on the standard list of enquiries; Tamhini has two term loans with the bank and directors who are shareholders.

options.text: Write to Tamhini’s lawyers about the pending cases
options.why: We ask management about pending cases instead. For a quarter, a letter to the lawyers usually isn’t needed.

options.text: Ask about events after 30 September, up to the date of our report
options.why: Anything up to the report date that needs adjusting or disclosing has to be asked about.

options.text: Vouch the purchase bills booked in the quarter
options.why: Vouching is audit work. In a review we ask and compare, and look for a paper only where something doesn’t fit.

options.text: Get the management representation letter for the quarter
options.why: Management confirms in writing that the uncorrected items we listed don’t matter, alone or together.

questions.sample: TC-35’s depreciation and the fee provision, left uncorrected: what now
questions.text: Mahesh replies on 30 October with Kudalwadi’s rate letter and the quantities, which settle the job-work query. TC-35’s depreciation and the fee provision, he says, are small, and he will deal with both at the year-end. What happens to those two now?

options.text: They come out of the file: each one is under our threshold, so neither can change the conclusion on the quarter.
options.why: The threshold decides what we look at, not what we record. A misstatement we found is listed and weighed with the others.

options.text: They go on our list of uncorrected misstatements; Sudha weighs them, alone and together, before she signs.
options.why: That is how a found error the client won’t fix is handled. The representation letter then lists them too.

options.text: The report says the results give a true and fair view except for the depreciation and the fee provision.
options.why: A review gives no audit opinion, and a qualified conclusion is for a material departure. Sudha decides that, and these two are small.

options.text: The report waits for the year-end audit, when both can be tested properly against the bills and the register.
options.why: The fund needs the reviewed results within 45 days. Known small errors don’t stop a review; they are recorded and weighed.

questions.text: Which sentence goes into the conclusion of Sudha’s review report on the quarter?

options.text: In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, the statement gives a true and fair view of the results of the company for the quarter.
options.why: That is an audit opinion. A review gives limited assurance and expresses no audit opinion.

options.text: Based on our audit of the books and records for the quarter, the statement of results is free from material misstatement and is fairly presented in accordance with the applicable accounting standards.
options.why: We did not audit the quarter, and a review never promises the results are free from misstatement.

options.text: Based on our review, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the statement is not prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable accounting standards.
options.why: This is the review conclusion. The two small errors we found don’t block it: the sentence says “in all material respects”, and Sudha has weighed them.

options.text: We certify that the statement of results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 is correct and complete in every respect, and that it agrees with the books of account of the company.
options.why: An auditor doesn’t certify results as correct. A review report states a conclusion and its basis.

wrap.text: Three queries, and two of them sit under our threshold: our fees and TC-35’s depreciation. Job work was the other kind, over the line with a reason that didn’t fit Q1. I’ll take the list to Rehan on Thursday.

wrapPartial.text: Over the threshold, a reason needs a paper that fits both comparisons; under it, ask what should have moved. And Sudha’s report gives a review conclusion, never an audit opinion. The list goes to Rehan when your file holds to those.

wrapRetry.text: Our rule is over 10% and over ₹10 lakh, against Q1 or last year. Test each reason against both comparisons and its papers. Then ask what should have moved but didn’t; the minutes, the asset schedule and our own fee letter show you where.

passNeeds.note: Your nine line calls need more right before this review can close.

model.intro: Five lines cross the threshold and have a paper that explains them. Finance costs is under it and moved as the loans say. Job work crosses it with a reason that doesn’t fit Q1, and two lines under it should have moved: our fees and depreciation.

rows.why: Vayuvega new (₹258.53 lakh); Kilimani two containers, not one
59.2% of manufactured sales, as in Q1
Units with production; cost per unit flat on Q1
A 1 July rate rise doesn’t show; no letter
Nil, against a provision every quarter last year
TC-35 ready 12 August, still in CWIP
Term loan I down ₹75 lakh; cash credit lower than Q1

blocks.text: TC-35’s missing depreciation, from 12 August to 30 September:

The threshold sorts the sheet; it doesn’t close it. Over the line with a paper behind it takes a minute. Under the line, ask what the minutes, the asset schedule and our own letter say should have moved.

principles: A threshold tells you where to look first, not what to ignore.
A client’s reason counts only when a paper shows it in both comparisons, Q1 and last year.
A review ends in a conclusion, “nothing has come to our attention”, not an audit opinion.

interview.q: What is a limited review, and how is it different from an audit?
interview.checking: Whether you know what a review does, and what it does not give.
outline: The statutory auditor’s review of interim results under SRE 2410: enquiries and analytical procedures.
In the simulation I set nine lines against Q1 and last year, then queried what didn’t fit.
